Retention time alignment via time warping

Source: R/correct_rt.R
correct_rt.Rd

Chromatograms are aligned using one of three algorithms, according to the value of alg: parametric time warping ("ptw"), as implemented in ptw; variable penalty dynamic time warping ("vpdtw"), as implemented in VPdtw; or landmark parametric time warping ("lptw"), which fits the warping polynomial directly to matched peak positions rather than full chromatographic signals.

Usage

correct_rt(
  chrom_list,
  lambdas,
  models = NULL,
  reference = "best",
  alg = c("ptw", "lptw", "vpdtw"),
  peaks = NULL,
  what = c("corrected.values", "models"),
  init.coef = c(0, 1, 0),
  n_traces = NULL,
  fill_zeros = FALSE,
  n_zeros = 0,
  scale = FALSE,
  trwdth = 0.2,
  plot_it = FALSE,
  penalty = 0.2,
  max_shift = 1,
  dilation_span = 0.3,
  rt_window = 0.3,
  spectral_cutoff = 0.95,
  regularization = 0,
  verbose = getOption("verbose"),
  show_progress = NULL,
  cl = 2,
  ...,
  n.traces = NULL,
  n.zeros = NULL,
  maxshift = NULL
)

Arguments

chrom_list

List of chromatograms in matrix format, sharing a common time axis (see preprocess).

lambdas

A character or numeric vector specifying the wavelengths to use for alignment. "vpdtw" and "lptw" accept only a single wavelength and raise an error otherwise. For one-dimensional chromatograms, this argument can be omitted.

models

List of models to warp by. The models provided here (if any) must match the algorithm selected in alg, and are matched to the samples of chrom_list by name.

reference

Index or name of the sample to be used as the reference. Fitted models record it by name. If not specified, chosen by bestref from a similarity matrix of the chromatograms.

alg

Alignment algorithm to use: parametric time warping ("ptw"), landmark parametric time warping ("lptw"), or variable penalty dynamic time warping ("vpdtw").

peaks

A peak list object from get_peaks or a matched_peak_list object from match_peaks. If a matched_peak_list is provided, peak matching will be skipped. Only used when alg = "lptw". If NULL, peaks are found with get_peaks and matched with match_peaks, both at their default settings. To change either, pass their output instead.

what

Output type: either the "corrected.values" (useful for visual inspection and downstream analysis) or the warping "models" (for further programmatic use).

init.coef

Starting values for the optimization. Named to match the argument of the same name in ptw, which receives it. For alg = "lptw", only its length is used, setting the degree of the warping polynomial.

n_traces

Number of wavelengths to warp by, chosen from lambdas (or from all wavelengths if lambdas is missing) by the CODA criterion in select.traces. Defaults to NULL, which uses every wavelength in lambdas.

fill_zeros

Logical. If TRUE, out-of-bounds regions produced by warping are filled with zeros; otherwise they are returned as NA (default).

n_zeros

Number of zeros to pad onto each end of the chromatograms before fitting. Only used when alg = "ptw".

scale

Logical. If TRUE, divide each chromatogram by its largest absolute value before fitting the warp, so that samples of very different concentration are matched on the shape of their signal. The corrected values are returned in their original units; to rescale the data themselves, use the maxI argument of preprocess. "ptw" is unaffected under its default criterion, weighted cross-correlation, which does not change when a sample is multiplied by a constant.

trwdth

Width of the triangle in the weighted cross-correlation (WCC) criterion, passed to ptw. Defaults to 0.2, which matches the default of 20 timepoints in ptw itself on a chromatogram sampled every 0.01 minutes. Roughly a peak width is a reasonable choice.

plot_it

Logical. Whether to plot alignment. Defaults to FALSE.

penalty

Numeric >= 0. Strength of the penalty against warping for alg = "vpdtw": the constant of proportionality in \(\lambda \propto\) dilation(reference) over a dilation_span-wide window, as recommended by Clifford and Stone (2012). A higher number allows less warping; 0 applies no penalty at all. Defaults to 0.2. In chromatographR <= 0.8.0 penalty was a divisor, so use the reciprocal of an old value. Values above 1 raise a warning, since they are more likely to be old divisors than deliberate choices.

max_shift

Maximum allowable shift for VPdtw warping, in minutes. Set it from the retention time drift you actually expect; the default of 1 allows a minute of drift. Although max_shift is a time, VPdtw itself works on the index axis, so the shift element of the returned models is reported in timepoints.

dilation_span

Width of the moving-maximum window used to build the "vpdtw" penalty. The penalty at each point is the largest reference intensity within dilation_span either side of it, computed by dilation after conversion to timepoints. Smaller values track individual peaks more closely, allowing more warping in the baseline between them. Larger values approach a constant penalty, which becomes exactly constant once dilation_span exceeds the distance between the tallest peak of the reference and the furthest end of the chromatogram. Defaults to 0.3, around a couple of peak widths on the example data.

rt_window

Numeric. Argument to match_peaks. Maximum allowed difference in retention time, in minutes, between a reference and sample peak to be considered a candidate match. Defaults to 0.3.

spectral_cutoff

Numeric. Argument to match_peaks. Minimum spectral correlation for a candidate peak pair to be retained. Defaults to 0.95.

regularization

Numeric >= 0. Strength of the penalty against warping for alg = "lptw": a dimensionless weight pulling the warp toward the identity warp, passed as penalty to fit_penalized_warp. A higher number allows less warping; 0 (the default) applies no penalty at all. 1 weights a unit of squared warp displacement equally against a unit of squared peak-position mismatch, and around 2.4 halves the applied warp, so useful values run roughly 0-10. Unbounded above, approaching the identity warp asymptotically.

verbose

Logical. Whether to print a progress message as the warping models are fit and applied. Defaults to getOption("verbose").

show_progress

Logical. Whether to show progress bar. Defaults to TRUE if pbapply is installed. Has no effect when alg = "vpdtw".

cl

Either an integer specifying the number of cores to use for parallel processing or a cluster object created by makeCluster. Defaults to 2. On Windows systems, integers are ignored. Has no effect when alg = "vpdtw".

...

For alg = "ptw", optional additional arguments passed to ptw. The only argument that cannot be changed is warp.type, which is hard-coded to "global" to permit warping on multiple wavelengths. For alg = "lptw", optional arguments passed to fit_penalized_warp: penalty_scale (per-coefficient penalty multipliers) and min_peaks (minimum matched peaks required to fit the polynomial). Its penalty argument is set by regularization rather than through ....

n.traces

The n.traces argument is deprecated. Please use n_traces instead.

n.zeros

The n.zeros argument is deprecated. Please use n_zeros instead.

maxshift

The maxshift argument is deprecated. Please use max_shift, which is in minutes. maxshift is read as a count of timepoints, as in chromatographR 0.8.0, and converted.

Value

A list of warping models or a list of warped absorbance profiles, according to the value of the what argument. With alg = "vpdtw", the warped chromatograms share a new time axis, which can be longer than the input.

Details

Some arguments are specific to particular warping functions. For example n_traces applies only to "ptw" warping; penalty, max_shift, and dilation_span apply only to "vpdtw" warping; and peaks, rt_window, spectral_cutoff, and regularization apply only to "lptw" warping.

trwdth, max_shift and dilation_span are widths along the time axis, given in minutes, regardless of the time unit of chrom_list, and rounded internally to a whole number of timepoints. trwdth was a count of timepoints up to chromatographR 0.8.0; multiply an old value by the sampling interval in minutes to convert it. A width wider than the chromatogram itself is rejected with an error, since it is almost certainly a stale timepoint count. max_shift replaces maxshift, which is still accepted as a count of timepoints.

regularization ("lptw") and penalty ("vpdtw") are not comparable: both are dimensionless and higher means less warping, but they are on unrelated scales.

Note

The PTW branch of correct_rt is adapted from the correctRT function in Ron Wehrens' alsace package.

References

  • Clifford, D., Stone, G., Montoliu, I., Rezzi, S., Martin, F. P., Guy, P., Bruce, S., & Kochhar, S. 2009. Alignment using variable penalty dynamic time warping. Analytical chemistry, 81(3):1000-1007. doi:10.1021/ac802041e .

  • Clifford, D., & Stone, G. 2012. Variable Penalty Dynamic Time Warping Code for Aligning Mass Spectrometry Chromatograms in R. Journal of Statistical Software, 47(8):1-17. doi:10.18637/jss.v047.i08 .

  • Eilers, P.H.C. 2004. Parametric Time Warping. Analytical Chemistry, 76:404-411. doi:10.1021/ac034800e .

  • Wehrens, R., Bloemberg, T.G., and Eilers P.H.C. 2015. Fast parametric time warping of peak lists. Bioinformatics, 31:3063-3065. doi:10.1093/bioinformatics/btv299 .

  • Wehrens, R., Carvalho, E., Fraser, P.D. 2015. Metabolite profiling in LC–DAD using multivariate curve resolution: the alsace package for R. Metabolomics, 11:143-154. doi:10.1007/s11306-014-0683-5 .
